'''Frank Verstraete''' (born November 1972<ref>{{cite web |url=http://congress.cimne.upc.es/rpmbt14/frontal/Kuemmel.asp |title=The Hermann Kümmel Early Achievement Award in Many-Body Physics |work=International Conference on Recent Progress in Many Body Theories |date=2007 |format=pdf |access-date=22 June 2021 |archive-date=5 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221005020740/http://congress.cimne.upc.es/rpmbt14/frontal/Kuemmel.asp }}</ref>) is a Belgian quantum physicist who is the Leigh Trapnell Professor of Quantum Physics at the [[Faculty of Mathematics, University of Cambridge]] and professor at the Faculty of Physics of [[Ghent University]]. He has worked on the interface between [[quantum information theory]] and quantum [[many-body physics]] and was an early proponent of the use of tensor networks and entanglement theory in quantum many body systems. A recurring theme of Verstraete's work is the reformulation of seemingly intractable problems in quantum physics as problems in linear algebra.

== Education and career ==
Verstraete was born in 1972, the son of Belgian doctors, and attended the {{ill|Abdijschool van Zevenkerken|nl}}.<ref name="j067">{{cite web | title=2018 – Rapport Frank Verstraete – Fondation Francqui – Stichting | website=Fondation Francqui – Stichting – Fondation d'Utilité Publique – Stichting van Openbaar Nut | date=2018-04-16 | url=https://www.francquifoundation.be/nederlands/francqui-prijs/laureaten/rapport-cherchye-de-rock-vermeulen-2/2018-rapport-frank-verstraete/ | language=fr }}</ref> He obtained a degree of electrical engineering in Louvain and of Master in Physics from Ghent University, and obtained his PhD on the topic of quantum entanglement in 2002 under supervision of Bart De Moor and Henri Verschelde at the [[KU Leuven]].<ref>{{cite book |title=A study of entanglement in quantum information theory |author=Frank Verstraete |publisher=Katholieke Universiteit Leuven |year=2002 |isbn=978-90-5682-377-1 |url=https://biblio.ugent.be/publication/8603813}}</ref> He pioneered the use of [[quantum entanglement]] as a unifying theme for describing strongly interacting quantum many-body systems, which are among the most challenging systems to analyze theoretically or numerically, but also very promising for future quantum technologies such as quantum computers.

From 2002 to 2004 he was a postdoctoral researcher at the [[Max Planck Institute for Quantum Optics]] in the group of [[Ignacio Cirac]] and from 2004 to 2006 he was a postdoctoral researcher at the [[California Institute of Technology]]. In 2006, he became full professor and the chair of theoretical quantum nanophysics at the [[University of Vienna]]. He moved back to Ghent University with an Odysseus grant from the [[Research Foundation – Flanders (FWO)|FWO]] in 2012, where he has since built a research group on applications of entanglement to quantum many-body systems. Since the fall of 2022, he holds the chair of Quantum Physics at the Department of Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Physics of the [[University of Cambridge]].

== Scientific work ==

Among his contributions to [[quantum information]] theory is the classification of the nine equivalence classes under stochastic local operations and classical communication (SLOCC) in which four [[qubit]]s can be entangled.<ref name="fourqubits">{{cite journal |last1=Verstraete |first1=F. |last2=Dehaene |first2=J. |last3=De Moor |first3=B. |last4=Verschelde |first4=H. |year=2002 |title=Four qubits can be entangled in nine different ways |journal=[[Physical Review A]] |volume=65 |issue=5 |article-number=052112 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.65.052112 |arxiv=quant-ph/0109033 |bibcode=2002PhRvA..65e2112V }}</ref> The underlying mathematical question, the classification of 2×2×2×2 tensors, is a classic problem in algebraic geometry: posed by [[Constantin Le Paige]] in 1881 and advanced by [[Corrado Segre]] in 1922 using geometric methods, it had resisted a solution by the advanced machinery of invariant theory.<ref name="lepaige">{{cite journal |last1=Luque |first1=J.-G. |last2=Thibon |first2=J.-Y. |year=2003 |title=Polynomial invariants of four qubits |journal=[[Physical Review A]] |volume=67 |issue=4 |article-number=042303 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.67.042303 |arxiv=quant-ph/0212069 |bibcode=2003PhRvA..67d2303L }}</ref> Verstraete solved it by recasting it as a simple problem in linear algebra, an approach that would set the tone for much of his later work. In a companion paper, he constructed normal forms for arbitrary multipartite quantum states, together with a constructive algorithm for bringing any tensor into its normal form;<ref name="normalforms">{{cite journal |last1=Verstraete |first1=F. |last2=Dehaene |first2=J. |last3=De Moor |first3=B. |year=2003 |title=Normal forms and entanglement measures for multipartite quantum states |journal=[[Physical Review A]] |volume=68 |issue=1 |article-number=012103 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.68.012103 |arxiv=quant-ph/0105090 |bibcode=2003PhRvA..68a2103V }}</ref> this algorithm was later used as a central primitive in the theory of tensor scaling, the multilinear generalisation of [[Sinkhorn's theorem|Sinkhorn's matrix scaling]], with applications ranging from invariant theory to computational complexity.<ref name="tensorscaling">{{cite conference |last1=Bürgisser |first1=P. |last2=Garg |first2=A. |last3=Oliveira |first3=R. |last4=Walter |first4=M. |last5=Wigderson |first5=A. |year=2018 |title=Alternating Minimization, Scaling Algorithms, and the Null-Cone Problem from Invariant Theory |book-title=9th Innovations in Theoretical Computer Science Conference (ITCS 2018) |series=Leibniz International Proceedings in Informatics |volume=94 |pages=24:1–24:20 |doi=10.4230/LIPIcs.ITCS.2018.24 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

Verstraete, together with Audenaert, also solved the long-standing open problem of symmetric and asymmetric quantum hypothesis testing by proving the quantum generalisations of the classical Chernoff and Hoeffding bounds, which characterise the optimal error exponents for discriminating quantum states.<ref name="chernoff">{{cite journal |last1=Audenaert |first1=K. M. R. |last2=Calsamiglia |first2=J. |last3=Muñoz-Tapia |first3=R. |last4=Bagan |first4=E. |last5=Masanes |first5=Ll. |last6=Acín |first6=A. |author-link6=Antonio Acín |last7=Verstraete |first7=F. |year=2007 |title=Discriminating States: The Quantum Chernoff Bound |journal=[[Physical Review Letters]] |volume=98 |issue=16 |article-number=160501 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.98.160501 |pmid=17501405 |arxiv=quant-ph/0610027 |bibcode=2007PhRvL..98p0501A }}</ref><ref name="hoeffding">{{cite journal |last1=Audenaert |first1=K. M. R. |last2=Nussbaum |first2=M. |last3=Szkoła |first3=A. |last4=Verstraete |first4=F. |year=2008 |title=Asymptotic Error Rates in Quantum Hypothesis Testing |journal=[[Communications in Mathematical Physics]] |volume=279 |issue=1 |pages=251–283 |doi=10.1007/s00220-008-0417-5 |arxiv=0708.4282 |bibcode=2008CMaPh.279..251A }}</ref> Together with Bravyi and [[Matthew Hastings|Hastings]], he introduced [[Lieb–Robinson bounds]] in the field of quantum information, proving that correlations and [[topological order|topological quantum order]] cannot be created by local Hamiltonian evolution in a time shorter than one proportional to the system size, establishing rigorous lower bounds on the time needed to prepare topologically ordered states.<ref name="liebrobinson">{{cite journal |last1=Bravyi |first1=S. |last2=Hastings |first2=M. B. |author-link2=Matthew Hastings |last3=Verstraete |first3=F. |year=2006 |title=Lieb-Robinson Bounds and the Generation of Correlations and Topological Quantum Order |journal=[[Physical Review Letters]] |volume=97 |issue=5 |article-number=050401 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.97.050401 |pmid=17026080 |arxiv=quant-ph/0603121 |bibcode=2006PhRvL..97e0401B }}</ref> He also laid the groundwork for the simulation of fermionic matter on a [[quantum computer]]: together with [[Ignacio Cirac|Cirac]], he introduced a local transformation mapping fermions to qubits, known as the Verstraete–Cirac transformation,<ref name="vcmapping">{{cite journal |last1=Verstraete |first1=F. |last2=Cirac |first2=J. I. |author-link2=Ignacio Cirac |year=2005 |title=Mapping local Hamiltonians of fermions to local Hamiltonians of spins |journal=[[Journal of Statistical Mechanics: Theory and Experiment]] |volume=2005 |issue=9 |page=09012 |doi=10.1088/1742-5468/2005/09/P09012 |arxiv=cond-mat/0508353 |bibcode=2005JSMTE..09..012V }}</ref> and he constructed the fermionic [[fast Fourier transform]] and related quantum circuits that form the basis for the quantum simulation of realistic materials.<ref name="ffft">{{cite journal |last1=Verstraete |first1=F. |last2=Cirac |first2=J. I. |last3=Latorre |first3=J. I. |year=2009 |title=Quantum circuits for strongly correlated quantum systems |journal=[[Physical Review A]] |volume=79 |issue=3 |article-number=032316 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.79.032316 |arxiv=0804.1888 |bibcode=2009PhRvA..79c2316V }}</ref> In three papers between 2009 and 2011, Verstraete established quantum Markov processes as a paradigm for quantum computation and many-body state preparation: together with Wolf and Cirac, he demonstrated that universal quantum computation can be realised entirely through dissipation,<ref name="dissipation">{{cite journal |last1=Verstraete |first1=F. |last2=Wolf |first2=M. M. |last3=Cirac |first3=J. I. |year=2009 |title=Quantum computation and quantum-state engineering driven by dissipation |journal=[[Nature Physics]] |volume=5 |issue=9 |pages=633–636 |doi=10.1038/nphys1342 |arxiv=0803.1447 |bibcode=2009NatPh...5..633V }}</ref> with Temme, he developed the χ²-divergence framework for bounding the mixing times of quantum Markov processes,<ref name="chisquared">{{cite journal |last1=Temme |first1=K. |last2=Kastoryano |first2=M. J. |last3=Ruskai |first3=M. B. |author-link3=Mary Beth Ruskai |last4=Wolf |first4=M. M. |last5=Verstraete |first5=F. |year=2010 |title=The χ²-divergence and mixing times of quantum Markov processes |journal=[[Journal of Mathematical Physics]] |volume=51 |issue=12 |page=122201 |doi=10.1063/1.3511335 |arxiv=1005.2358}}</ref> and developed a quantum generalisation of the classical [[Metropolis–Hastings algorithm|Metropolis algorithm]] for preparing thermal states and finding ground states of many-body Hamiltonians.<ref name="metropolis">{{cite journal |last1=Temme |first1=K. |last2=Osborne |first2=T. J. |last3=Vollbrecht |first3=K. G. |last4=Poulin |first4=D. |last5=Verstraete |first5=F. |year=2011 |title=Quantum Metropolis sampling |journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]] |volume=471 |issue=7336 |pages=87–90 |doi=10.1038/nature09770 |pmid=21368829 |arxiv=0911.3635 |bibcode=2011Natur.471...87T }}</ref>

Verstraete has been centrally involved in the development of [[tensor network]]s since their inception, and the resulting variational methods define the state of the art for simulating strongly interacting quantum many-body systems. With [[Ignacio Cirac]] he introduced projected entangled pair states (PEPS), the generalisation of [[matrix product state]]s (MPS) to two and higher dimensions, in a 2004 preprint that was never formally published yet became one of the founding documents of the field.<ref name="peps">{{cite arXiv |last1=Verstraete |first1=F. |last2=Cirac |first2=J. I. |year=2004 |title=Renormalization algorithms for Quantum-Many Body Systems in two and higher dimensions |eprint=cond-mat/0407066 }}</ref> These methods rest on the insight that ground states of local Hamiltonians obey an entanglement area law, and therefore occupy an exponentially small corner of [[Hilbert space]] which tensor networks parameterise efficiently; Verstraete and Cirac made this precise by proving that ground states of gapped local Hamiltonians are faithfully represented by MPS with a bond dimension that does not grow with system size, providing the rigorous justification for the [[density matrix renormalization group]].<ref name="faithful">{{cite journal |last1=Verstraete |first1=F. |last2=Cirac |first2=J. I. |year=2006 |title=Matrix product states represent ground states faithfully |journal=[[Physical Review B]] |volume=73 |issue=9 |article-number=094423 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.73.094423 |arxiv=cond-mat/0505140 |bibcode=2006PhRvB..73i4423V }}</ref> They extended the framework to finite temperature and dissipation through matrix product density operators,<ref name="mpdo">{{cite journal |last1=Verstraete |first1=F. |last2=García-Ripoll |first2=J. J. |last3=Cirac |first3=J. I. |year=2004 |title=Matrix Product Density Operators: Simulation of Finite-Temperature and Dissipative Systems |journal=[[Physical Review Letters]] |volume=93 |issue=20 |article-number=207204 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.93.207204 |pmid=15600964 |arxiv=cond-mat/0406426 |bibcode=2004PhRvL..93t7204V }}</ref> and to the continuum through continuous MPS for quantum fields.<ref name="cmps">{{cite journal |last1=Verstraete |first1=F. |last2=Cirac |first2=J. I. |year=2010 |title=Continuous Matrix Product States for Quantum Fields |journal=[[Physical Review Letters]] |volume=104 |issue=19 |article-number=190405 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.104.190405 |pmid=20866951 |arxiv=1002.1824 |bibcode=2010PhRvL.104s0405V }}</ref> Because tensor network states form a smooth manifold rather than a linear space, the natural language for dynamics on them is that of [[tangent space]]s: with Haegeman he exploited this geometric structure to construct a variational ansatz for elementary excitations on top of an MPS<ref name="excitations">{{cite journal |last1=Haegeman |first1=J. |last2=Pirvu |first2=B. |last3=Weir |first3=D. J. |last4=Cirac |first4=J. I. |last5=Osborne |first5=T. J. |last6=Verschelde |first6=H. |last7=Verstraete |first7=F. |year=2012 |title=Variational matrix product ansatz for dispersion relations |journal=[[Physical Review B]] |volume=85 |issue=10 |article-number=100408 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.85.100408 |arxiv=1103.2286 |bibcode=2012PhRvB..85j0408H }}</ref> and a time-dependent variational principle that unifies real-time evolution and ground-state optimisation on the same manifold.<ref name="tdvp">{{cite journal |last1=Haegeman |first1=J. |last2=Cirac |first2=J. I. |last3=Osborne |first3=T. J. |last4=Pižorn |first4=I. |last5=Verschelde |first5=H. |last6=Verstraete |first6=F. |year=2011 |title=Time-Dependent Variational Principle for Quantum Lattices |journal=[[Physical Review Letters]] |volume=107 |issue=7 |article-number=070601 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.107.070601 |pmid=21902379 |arxiv=1103.0936 |bibcode=2011PhRvL.107g0601H }}</ref><ref name="unifying">{{cite journal |last1=Haegeman |first1=J. |last2=Lubich |first2=C. |last3=Oseledets |first3=I. |last4=Vandereycken |first4=B. |last5=Verstraete |first5=F. |year=2016 |title=Unifying time evolution and optimization with matrix product states |journal=[[Physical Review B]] |volume=94 |issue=16 |article-number=165116 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.94.165116 |arxiv=1408.5056 |bibcode=2016PhRvB..94p5116H }}</ref>

A second strand of his work on [[tensor network]]s treats the local tensor not as a numerical approximation but as an object of study in its own right: whether the particles of a phase are fermions, whether it is topologically ordered and which symmetries it supports are all fixed by the symmetry algebra of a small array of numbers repeated across the lattice. That this is even well defined rests on what Verstraete coined the "fundamental theorem of MPS" — the statement that any two local tensors generating the same state are related by a gauge transformation — which underpins most structural results on matrix product states, including the classification of symmetry-protected topological phases in one dimension.<ref name="fundamentaltheorem">{{cite journal |last1=Cirac |first1=J. I. |last2=Pérez-García |first2=D. |last3=Schuch |first3=N. |last4=Verstraete |first4=F. |year=2021 |title=Matrix product states and projected entangled pair states: Concepts, symmetries, theorems |journal=[[Reviews of Modern Physics]] |volume=93 |issue=4 |article-number=045003 |doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.93.045003 |arxiv=2011.12127 |bibcode=2021RvMP...93d5003C }}</ref> Fermionic statistics, for instance, can be built directly into the network, either through fermionic PEPS, developed with Kraus, Schuch and Cirac,<ref name="fpeps">{{cite journal |last1=Kraus |first1=C. V. |last2=Schuch |first2=N. |last3=Verstraete |first3=F. |last4=Cirac |first4=J. I. |year=2010 |title=Fermionic projected entangled pair states |journal=[[Physical Review A]] |volume=81 |issue=5 |article-number=052338 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.81.052338 |arxiv=0904.4667 |bibcode=2010PhRvA..81e2338K }}</ref> or through tensor networks over graded vector spaces, in which the fermionic sign structure is carried by the grading itself.<ref name="graded">{{cite journal |last1=Bultinck |first1=N. |last2=Williamson |first2=D. J. |last3=Haegeman |first3=J. |last4=Verstraete |first4=F. |year=2018 |title=Fermionic projected entangled-pair states and topological phases |journal=[[Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and Theoretical]] |volume=51 |issue=2 |page=025202 |doi=10.1088/1751-8121/aa99cc |arxiv=1707.00470 |bibcode=2018JPhA...51b5202B }}</ref> Starting in 2014, Verstraete and his collaborators showed that topological order in tensor networks is characterised by algebras of matrix product operators (MPOs) acting on the virtual degrees of freedom, from which the anyonic excitations of the phase can be constructed explicitly.<ref name="mpochar">{{cite journal |last1=Şahinoğlu |first1=M. B. |last2=Williamson |first2=D. |last3=Bultinck |first3=N. |last4=Mariën |first4=M. |last5=Haegeman |first5=J. |last6=Schuch |first6=N. |last7=Verstraete |first7=F. |year=2021 |orig-date=2014 |title=Characterizing Topological Order with Matrix Product Operators |journal=[[Annales Henri Poincaré]] |volume=22 |issue=2 |pages=563–592 |doi=10.1007/s00023-020-00992-4 |arxiv=1409.2150 |bibcode=2021AnHP...22..563S }}</ref><ref name="mpoanyons">{{cite journal |last1=Bultinck |first1=N. |last2=Mariën |first2=M. |last3=Williamson |first3=D. J. |last4=Şahinoğlu |first4=M. B. |last5=Haegeman |first5=J. |last6=Verstraete |first6=F. |year=2017 |title=Anyons and matrix product operator algebras |journal=[[Annals of Physics]] |volume=378 |pages=183–233 |doi=10.1016/j.aop.2017.01.004 |arxiv=1511.08090 |bibcode=2017AnPhy.378..183B }}</ref> This revealed that topological order — introduced by [[Xiao-Gang Wen]] as physics beyond the Landau paradigm of symmetry breaking, and epitomised by the exactly solvable models of [[Alexei Kitaev]] — is, after all, still a story of symmetries and their breaking, albeit generalised symmetries that are only visible through the entanglement degrees of freedom which form the central object of tensor network theory.<ref name="mpochar" /><ref name="freiberger">{{cite web |last=Freiberger |first=M. |date=2 March 2026 |title=New phases of matter: Abstract nonsense comes good |website=[[Plus Magazine]] |publisher=Isaac Newton Institute |url=https://plus.maths.org/new-phases-matter}}</ref> With Lootens and Delcamp, these MPO algebras were subsequently promoted to a systematic theory of generalised symmetries and dualities of quantum lattice models, in which the duality transformations themselves are realised as explicit MPO intertwiners.<ref name="dualities">{{cite journal |last1=Lootens |first1=L. |last2=Delcamp |first2=C. |last3=Ortiz |first3=G. |last4=Verstraete |first4=F. |year=2023 |title=Dualities in One-Dimensional Quantum Lattice Models: Symmetric Hamiltonians and Matrix Product Operator Intertwiners |journal=[[PRX Quantum]] |volume=4 |issue=2 |article-number=020357 |doi=10.1103/PRXQuantum.4.020357 |arxiv=2112.09091 |bibcode=2023PRXQ....4b0357L }}</ref> This body of work provided an early lattice realisation of the categorical structures — fusion categories, module categories and their associators — that underlie the present-day symmetry topological field theory (SymTFT) description of generalised symmetries.<ref name="freiberger" /><ref name="stringnets">{{cite journal |last1=Lootens |first1=L. |last2=Fuchs |first2=J. |last3=Haegeman |first3=J. |last4=Schweigert |first4=C. |last5=Verstraete |first5=F. |year=2021 |title=Matrix product operator symmetries and intertwiners in string-nets |journal=[[SciPost Physics]] |volume=10 |issue=3 |page=053 |doi=10.21468/SciPostPhys.10.3.053 |doi-access=free |arxiv=2008.11187}}</ref>


== Awards ==
Verstraete has received numerous awards, among them the Hermann Kümmel early achievement award in many-body physics, the [[Lieben Prize]] in 2009<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.derstandard.at/story/1256744203340/ignaz-l-lieben-preis-an-frank-verstraete |title=Ignaz L. Lieben-Preis 2009 an Frank Verstraete |work=Der Standard |date = 6 November 2009 |language=de |access-date=22 June 2021}}</ref> and the [[Francqui Prize]] in 2018<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.oeaw.ac.at/esq/home/news-detail/frank-verstraete-awarded-prestigious-franqui-prize |title=Frank Verstraete awarded prestigious Franqui Prize |date=15 June 2018 |work=Austrian Academy of Sciences |access-date=22 June 2021}}</ref> and is also distinguished visiting research chair at the [[Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics]] in [[Waterloo, Ontario]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ugent.be/en/research/research-ugent/trackrecord/trackrecord-h2020/erc-h2020/erc-frank-verstraete.htm|title=Frank Verstraete – QUTE — Ghent University|website=www.ugent.be|language=en|access-date=19 May 2018|archive-date=16 January 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190116083617/https://www.ugent.be/en/research/research-ugent/trackrecord/trackrecord-h2020/erc-h2020/erc-frank-verstraete.htm}}</ref>

== Books ==
Together with [[Céline Broeckaert]], he wrote the popular science book ''Why Nobody Understands Quantum Physics'' ([[Pan Books]]).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.standard.co.uk/culture/books/why-nobody-understands-quantum-physics-frank-verstraete-celine-broeckaert-b1230150.html |title=Why you need to fall in love with quantum physics — before the next revolution |work= the Standard |date = 29 May 2025 |language=en |access-date=29 May 2025 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book | last1=Verstraete | first1=Frank | last2=Broeckaert | first2=Céline | title=Why Nobody Understands Quantum Physics: And Everyone Needs to Know Something About It | date=5 June 2025 | publisher=Pan Macmillan | isbn=978-1-0350-6585-1 }}</ref> Waterstones included ''Why Nobody Understands Quantum Physics'' in its selection of the 2025 best popular-science books.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.waterstones.com/blog/the-best-popular-science-books-of-2025 |title=The Best Popular Science Books of 2025 |website=Waterstones |access-date=28 July 2026}}</ref> The book has been published in eight languages.

== Personal life ==
Verstraete is married to [[Céline Broeckaert]].<ref name="f854">{{cite web | title=#72 Céline Broeckaert and Frank Verstraete | website=Isaac Newton Institute | date=2025-11-12 | url=https://www.newton.ac.uk/media/podcasts/post/72-living-proof-celine-broeckaert-and-frank-verstraete/ }}</ref>
